Fact.Name: Form 4562 Part III Section C classification rows

Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part I line 11, the smaller of the taxpayer's aggregate taxable income from the active conduct of a trade or business (not less than zero) and line 5. Fact.Name: The return level section 179 allocation is in force for this Form 4562
Fact.Description:
True when more than one activity on the return elects section 179 (scheduleE:/hasMultipleSection179ElectingActivities) AND the allocation guard scheduleE:/knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities is DOWN, i.e. every electing rental element and every electing K-1 has a resolving row of scheduleE:/section179AllocationByActivity and the shares fit the taxpayer's line 5 and line 11 limits. That is exactly the population on which the Line 12 instruction's "Summary" division exists: "if you have more than one business or activity, you may allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them".
WHY THE GUARD AND NOT THE COVERAGE FLAGS DIRECTLY: the guard is the one fact that already conjoins both arms' coverage with the fits check, and reading it keeps this module's edge into scheduleE to the two facts it already had the direction for (form4562 reads scheduleE; scheduleE reads nothing from form4562). A single elector who answered the allocation anyway has nothing to allocate and is false here, as it is for the rental deduction's allocated arm. A refused multi elector return is false here, so Part I keeps printing its own table chain on a return that cannot be filed.
TYPE: Boolean, always Complete: both operands are always Complete Booleans (the flag by construction, the guard by its own Description). Read by /knockoutSection179AllocationDoesNotDivideSummaryLine12, which checks that the allocation divides the Summary line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 12 lines 9 and 10 before the business income limitation
Fact.Description:

ON A MULTI-ACTIVITY RETURN THIS IS THE SUMMARY. The instructions put the totals for all businesses and activities on a "Summary" Form 4562, whose Part I is the ordinary computation (line 9 from the line 6 table, which carries a partner's or shareholder's Schedule K-1 share as its own row), and they divide the Summary's allowable deduction among the activities on each activity's line 12. So the allocation the filer enters (scheduleE:/section179AllocationByActivity) does not replace line 9 here: it must divide the line 12 this chain produces, and a return whose allocation does not is refused by /knockoutSection179AllocationDoesNotDivideSummaryLine12.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 7, listed property elected cost as the form computes it
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 7, "Listed property. Enter the amount from line 29". It IS the Part V line 29 total (/form4562Line29ElectedSection179CostTotal), and on a return that entered no listed property at all it is zero. /form4562Line8TotalElectedCost adds it, line 8 goes to line 9, line 9 to line 12, and line 12 is the section 179 deduction that reaches the return.
THE FORM ALLOWS LINE 7 NO OTHER SOURCE. The Part I note reads "If you have any listed property, complete Part V before you complete Part I", the line 6 instruction sends the elected cost of listed property to column (i) of line 26 and nowhere else, and line 29 says "Enter here and on line 7, page 1". A nonzero line 7 with no line 26 row is therefore not a return this form can print: whatever the amount is, the property it belongs to is listed property, and listed property that is expensed under section 179 has a Part V row.
WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE CONVENIENCE IT COSTS. Every ceiling on a section 179 election of listed property lives on the Part V row — the row's own business-use cost, the section 179(b)(5) sport utility vehicle amount, the section 280F(a) passenger-automobile limit, and the section 280F(b) denial to property not predominantly used in a qualified business use. A line 7 that could be answered directly is a route around all four at once, and the larger the improper election the more it is worth taking. The amount a filer would have typed here is entered as a Part V row instead, where the law can reach it.
COMPLETE-SAFE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A return that never initialised the listed-property collection resolves to zero rather than to a Placeholder, so line 8 and the whole section 179 chain stay resolvable on every return that carries no Part V; a return with a Part V table takes the computed total. /writableForm4562Line7ListedPropertyElectedCost keeps its path and its meaning for intake that has already collected it, but nothing on the return reads it.

Fact.Name: Section 179 property elected on Form 4562 line 6
Fact.Description:
One item per item of section 179 property for which the taxpayer makes the election, printed as a line 6 row of the Form 4562 Part I table: column (a) description, column (b) cost (business use only), column (c) elected cost. IRC 179(c)(1) requires the election to specify the items and the portion of each item's cost taken into account, which is what these rows are. The register prints the first two rows (see the IRS4562 /form4562Section179Properties rows axis); listed property is excluded from line 6 and reaches Part I through line 7.
ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT: one section 179 election was enterable in three places: this table, scheduleE:/rentalProperties/*/fiveYearSection179ElectedCost and scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableSection179Deduction. THIS TABLE IS THE PRINTED PART I LINE 6 ITEMISATION, the "items of section 179 property to which the election applies and the portion of the cost of each of such items" IRC 179(c)(1)(A) requires the election to specify. It is an INPUT to the taxpayer level allocation, not a rival answer to it. The rental election stays the Schedule E writable and the K-1 box 12 figure stays the K-1 transcription; the SHARE of the one taxpayer dollar limit is entered in exactly one place, the return level collection scheduleE:/section179AllocationByActivity. SEQUENCED, not built here: /form4562Line12Section179Deduction still reads this table's own chain rather than that allocation, so on a return that carries both a Schedule E rental election and rows here the two are not yet reconciled. Line 12 is print only today, so the divergence moves no tax; /form4562Line12BeforeIncomeLimitation reads the allocation's entered share total whenever /form4562Section179AllocationInForce (more than one electing activity and the allocation guard down), and the table chain otherwise. What remains unreconciled is the table against the Schedule E elections themselves, named on that fact.

Fact.Name: Section 179 elected cost for one line 6 row, bounded by that row's own cost
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 6 column (c) for one elected item, as the law allows it to stand: the filer's entry, except that an entry exceeding the same row's column (b) cost resolves to that cost. IRC 179(c)(1)(A) requires the election to specify "the portion of the cost of such property" the taxpayer takes into account, so an amount larger than the item's own cost is not a bigger election — beyond the cost there is no portion left to elect, and the deduction IRC 179(a) allows is capped at the cost of the property in any event. /form4562Line6ElectedCostTotal sums THIS fact, not the raw column (c) writable, which is what keeps an over-entry out of line 8, line 9 and line 12.
THE CAP FIRES ONLY ON AN AFFIRMATIVE CONTRADICTION, and it is complete-safe. Both intakes must be answered AND column (c) must be strictly greater than column (b) before the cap arm is taken; equal entries and every ordinary entry fall through to the writable term for term, and a row with either intake unanswered passes the writable's own Incomplete through unchanged, so line 6's completeness does not move on any return. BYTE IDENTICAL ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: no committed scenario carries a column (c) entry above its column (b).
THE LISTED-PROPERTY TWIN IS BUILT, on /form4562ListedProperties/*/electedCostWithinBusinessUseCost. Part V column (i) had the same unbounded shape against the business-use portion of column (d), and the operand that bound needs — column (d) multiplied by the column (c) business-use percentage — is now /form4562ListedProperties/*/businessUseCostOrOtherBasis. It is deliberately not column (e): i4562 defines column (e) as that same product REDUCED BY the section 179 deduction itself, so bounding (i) by (e) would be circular.
STILL NAMED: the printed register binds the raw column (c) writables, so on the contradictory return the printed rows and the printed line 6 total disagree until the IRS4562 register rows are re-pointed at this fact.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 25 special depreciation allowance for listed property
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part V Section A line 25, the IRC 168(k) additional first year allowance for qualified listed property placed in service during the tax year: the SUM of the per-row shares at /form4562ListedProperties/*/specialDepreciationAllowanceShare. The box sits in column (h), so line 28 adds it to the column (h) amounts of lines 26 and 27, and line 28 is Part IV line 21.
IT IS COMPUTED, NOT COLLECTED. The instructions say to enter on line 25 the taxpayer's TOTAL special depreciation allowance for all qualified listed property, and Part V Section A is where that property is listed property by property, so every dollar on this line belongs to a row of the same table. While line 25 was a separate intake (/writableForm4562Line25ListedPropertySpecialAllowance, now retired) a return could state a total its own rows did not add to, and the arithmetic no one could check was the same arithmetic the section 280F(a) cap depends on: /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnIRemainingLimit subtracts the row's own share from that row's limit, so a stated total and an unrelated set of shares could over- and under-cap the same automobile at once. One figure now feeds both.
COMPLETE-SAFE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, the line 7 idiom this module already uses. A return that never initialised the listed-property collection resolves to $0 rather than a Placeholder, so line 28, line 21 and line 22 stay resolvable on every return that carries no Part V; a row that took no allowance adds nothing, so a Part V table nobody asked the allowance question about still totals. The line can only be as large as the shares the rows state, and it is Incomplete for want of an answer in exactly one place: a row on which the filer answered yes to claiming the allowance and left the amount blank, where the share has no case and this total waits for it rather than printing a figure that omits an allowance the filer said was taken.
ONLY PROPERTY USED MORE THAN 50 PERCENT IN A QUALIFIED BUSINESS USE CONTRIBUTES, which is what the printed line says on its face and what IRC 280F(b)(1) with 168(k)(2)(D) requires: a row whose /form4562ListedProperties/*/isPredominantlyBusinessUse resolves false has a share of $0 whatever amount was entered on it, so this total cannot grow by an allowance the law denies.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 28 listed property depreciation total
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part V Section A line 28: the column (h) amounts of lines 25 through 27 added together, which is the line 25 special depreciation allowance plus the column (h) total of the line 26 and line 27 rows. The form carries it to Part IV line 21.
BOTH ADDENDS ARE COMPUTED FROM THE PART V TABLE and both are complete-safe on a return with no listed property, so this total is too. Line 25 is /form4562Line25ListedPropertySpecialAllowance, the sum of the rows' allowance shares, and NOT the retired /writableForm4562Line25ListedPropertySpecialAllowance intake, which nothing reads.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 29 elected section 179 cost of listed property
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part V Section A line 29: the column (i) total of line 26, the cost of listed property the taxpayer elects to expense under IRC 179, which the form carries to Part I line 7. It is the total the return acts on — /form4562Line7ListedPropertyElectedCost is this figure on any return that carries a Part V row, line 8 adds it, and line 12 is the section 179 deduction that reaches the return.
IT SUMS THE CAPPED PER-ROW AMOUNT, /form4562ListedProperties/*/electedSection179CostAllowed, and not the raw column (i) intake. Four ceilings are inside that fact — the row's own business-use cost, the section 179(b)(5) sport utility vehicle amount, what is left of the section 280F(a) passenger-automobile limit after column (h), and zero on a row not predominantly used in a qualified business use — so no ceiling has to be restated here and none can be reached around.
THE SUM RUNS OVER THE WHOLE COLLECTION, which is right because the per-row fact already zeroes every row the printed line 26 block would not accept. The printed table's six slots are a positional convention (line 26 rows at items 0 to 2, line 27 rows at items 3 to 5) and intake is expected to honour it, but this total does not depend on it: a row whose column (c) is 50 percent or less contributes nothing wherever it sits, and a row above 50 percent contributes wherever it sits. Property used 50 percent or less in a qualified business use may not be expensed under section 179 at all, and its printed row carries no column (i) box.
NAMED, NOT BUILT HERE: the printed rows themselves. The IRS4562 register binds the raw column (i) writables by slot, so on a return whose entries the caps cut down, the printed rows and this printed total disagree until those register rows are re-pointed at the capped fact.

Fact.Name: Written policy prohibiting all personal use of vehicles: No
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 37: the negation of the line 37 attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: Written policy prohibiting personal use except commuting: No
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 38: the negation of the line 38 attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: All employee vehicle use treated as personal use: No
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 39: the negation of the line 39 attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: More than five vehicles provided and use information retained: No
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 40: the negation of the line 40 attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: Qualified automobile demonstration use requirements met: No
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 41: the negation of the line 41 attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 42 column (f): Schedule C business start-up amortization that begins this year
Fact.Description: The sum over every Schedule C business of its IRC 195(b)(1)(B) ratable amortization for this year (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/startUpExpendituresAmortizationDeduction): the start-up expenditures left after the first-year deduction, over 180 months from the month the business began. It is above $0 only for a business that began this year, which is exactly the amortization line 42 reports ("amortization period begins during your tax year"). The first-year deduction of up to $5,000 is a deduction, not amortization, and is not here. Complete safe $0 when no Schedule C is listed. Added to /form4562Line42ColumnFTotal, so line 44 carries it; Schedule C already deducts it in Part V (line 48), so nothing here moves tax.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 42 column (f) total
Fact.Description: The column (f) total of Form 4562 line 42: the amortization allowable this year for the costs whose amortization begins during the tax year. The filer's line 42 rows plus the Schedule C business start-up amortization the return computes (/form4562Line42ScheduleCStartUpAmortization), which the rows must not repeat. Complete safe zero when neither is present.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 44 total amortization
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 44: the total of column (f), the line 42 amortization plus the line 43 amortization of costs that began before this tax year. Print only until a Schedule C other expenses consumer reads it, so the amortization deduction reaches the return.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's section 280F(a) first-year limit, prorated by column (c)
Fact.Description:
The whole of the IRC 280F(a) pool for this row when it is a passenger automobile placed in service in 2025: the Table 2 first-year limit, $12,200, or $20,200 where the taxpayer takes the special depreciation allowance on a row used more than 50 percent in a qualified business use, multiplied by the column (c) business/investment use percentage. For any passenger automobile the total of columns (h) and (i) on line 26 or 27 and column (h) on line 25 cannot exceed this figure.
THE $20,200 FIGURE NEEDS THE ALLOWANCE. A row used 50 percent or less in a qualified business use takes no special depreciation allowance (IRC 280F(b)(1) with 168(k)(2)(D)), so it takes the $12,200 figure; so does a row whose predominance is not yet known, which is the figure that cannot overstate the deduction.
Read by /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnHLimit (what the pool leaves column (h) once the line 25 share is taken) and /form4562ListedProperties/*/specialDepreciationAllowanceShare (the line 25 share itself may not exceed the pool). Incomplete until column (c) is answered.

Fact.Name: What a Part V row's section 280F(a) limit leaves for its column (h) depreciation
Fact.Description:
The ceiling IRC 280F(a) sets on this row's column (h) depreciation deduction when the row is a passenger automobile placed in service in 2025: the prorated first-year limit (/form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FFirstYearLimit) less the row's own line 25 special depreciation allowance (/form4562ListedProperties/*/specialDepreciationAllowanceShare), and never below zero.
ONE POOL. For a passenger automobile the total of columns (h) and (i) on line 26 or 27 and column (h) on line 25 cannot exceed the applicable limit. Column (h) takes what the line 25 allowance leaves; /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnIRemainingLimit gives column (i) what column (h) and line 25 leave. The line 25 share is itself held within the pool, so what is left here is never negative before the floor.
A claimed allowance with no amount leaves the share, and this fact, Incomplete.
Read only by /form4562ListedProperties/*/depreciationDeductionWithin280FCap, which applies it only to a row attested a passenger automobile and placed in service in 2025.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's section 280F(a) limit for a passenger automobile placed in service before 2025, prorated by column (c)
Fact.Description:
The IRC 280F(a) ceiling on the 2025 column (h) depreciation of a passenger automobile placed in service from 1987 through 2024 (a later tax year of its recovery, or the unrecovered basis after it), multiplied by the column (c) business/investment use percentage. The limit is fixed by the year the automobile was placed in service; a calendar-year return counts the tax years in service as 2025 less that year plus one, so a 2024 automobile is in its 2nd year ($19,800), a 2023 automobile its 3rd ($11,700), and every earlier one its 4th or later year.
SOURCES BY YEAR. 2004 to 2024: the 2025 Instructions for Form 4562 Tables 1 to 4, which Pub. 946 (2025) prints too. Electric passenger automobiles placed in service after August 5, 1997, and before 2007 take Pub. 946 (2025)'s electric-vehicle table (2004 to 2006) and Pub. 946 (2004)'s (1997 to 2003): $5,225 (2006, 2003), $5,125 (2004, 2005), $5,325 (1999 to 2002), $5,425 (August 6, 1997 to 1998). 2003: Pub. 946 (2004), $1,975 for a truck or van and $1,775 otherwise. 1997 to 2002: $1,775 (trucks and vans are passenger automobiles in that table). Before the electric exception: Pub. 946 (1998), $1,775 (1995 to August 5, 1997), $1,675 (1993, 1994) and $1,575 (Pre-1993, read as 1987 to 1992, the years MACRS applies). The two prior-year editions are vendored because the 2025 edition no longer prints those years; the figures do not change once the automobile is placed in service.
THE QUESTIONS IT NEEDS. /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsElectricVehicle for an automobile placed in service August 6, 1997 through 2006, and /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsTruckOrVan for a non-electric one placed in service 2003 through 2017. NO CATCH-ALL: a row whose needed answer or column (c) is blank resolves to nothing. A row placed in service before 1987 is refused instead (/knockoutPassengerAutomobilePlacedInServiceBefore1987).

Fact.Name: A Part V passenger automobile placed in service August 6, 1997 through 2006 runs primarily on electricity
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Was this vehicle produced to run primarily on electricity?" HELP TEXT: electric passenger automobiles placed in service after August 5, 1997, and before January 1, 2007, have their own, higher depreciation limits (Publication 946), and Table 3 of the Form 4562 instructions excludes them. ASKED WHEN: /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsPassengerAutomobile is yes and /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableDatePlacedInService falls from August 6, 1997 through December 31, 2006. UNANSWERED POSTURE: on that population /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FLaterYearLimit, the row's column (h) after the cap and line 28 are Incomplete (refused until answered). VALIDATION: Boolean. WHAT IT FEEDS: /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FLaterYearLimit.

Fact.Name: A Part V passenger automobile placed in service 2004 to 2017 is a truck or van
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Is this vehicle a truck or van?" HELP TEXT: for a passenger automobile placed in service from 2003 through 2017, the depreciation limit for 2025 depends on whether it is a truck or van: the Form 4562 instructions print one table for trucks and vans placed in service after 2003 and before 2018 (Table 4) and another for other passenger automobiles, which excludes trucks and vans placed in service after 2002 (Table 3); Pub. 946 (2004) prints the 2003 truck-and-van row. ASKED WHEN: /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsPassengerAutomobile is yes, /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableDatePlacedInService falls from January 1, 2003 through December 31, 2017, and the vehicle is not an electric vehicle placed in service before 2007 (/form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsElectricVehicle). UNANSWERED POSTURE: on that population /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FLaterYearLimit, the row's column (h) after the cap, and line 28 are Incomplete (refused until answered); never asked elsewhere. VALIDATION: Boolean. WHAT IT FEEDS: /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FLaterYearLimit.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's column (h) depreciation after the section 280F(a) passenger-automobile limit
Fact.Description:
The column (h) depreciation deduction line 28 adds for this row. On a row the taxpayer attests is a passenger automobile placed in service in 2025, a column (h) entry above /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnHLimit resolves to that limit. Every other row passes its column (h) entry through, floored at $0.
FIVE CASES, NO CATCH-ALL. 0. A column (h) entry of $0 or less: $0, since it cannot exceed any limit. 1. Attested passenger automobile, placed in service in 2025, column (c) answered, and column (h) above the limit: the limit. 2. Not attested a passenger automobile (unanswered or no): column (h) as entered. 3. Attested passenger automobile placed in service 1987 to 2024: capped at /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FLaterYearLimit, the later-year limit for its placed-in-service year; placed in service before 1987: column (h) as entered here, and the return is refused by /knockoutPassengerAutomobilePlacedInServiceBefore1987. 4. Attested passenger automobile placed in service in 2025 whose limit resolves and whose column (h) does not exceed it: column (h) as entered. An attested passenger automobile whose electric-vehicle (1997 to 2006) or truck-or-van (2003 to 2017) question is blank, or one with column (b) or column (c) blank, or a claimed special allowance with no amount, matches no case and is Incomplete rather than carrying an uncapped figure to line 28.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 lines 26 and 27 column (h) total
Fact.Description: The sum of column (h) over every printed listed property row, the line 26 and line 27 half of the line 28 total, each row read through /form4562ListedProperties/*/depreciationDeductionWithin280FCap so a 2025 passenger automobile carries no more than its section 280F(a) limit. Complete safe zero on an answered but empty collection.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 Part V listed property rows
Fact.Description: The listed property rows of Form 4562 Part V Section A: automobiles, certain other vehicles, certain aircraft, and property used for entertainment, recreation or amusement. The printed table is TWO blocks of three FIXED SLOTS: line 26 rows 1 to 3 hold property used more than 50 percent in a qualified business use and line 27 rows 1 to 3 hold property used 50 percent or less. One item per printed slot in that order, so items 0 to 2 are the line 26 rows and items 3 to 5 are the line 27 rows; an item is left blank when the slot is unused. The positional convention is what the IRS4562 /form4562ListedProperties rows column axis declares, and intake must create the slots in that order.

Fact.Name: Alternative depreciation system required for a Part V row
Fact.Description:
True exactly when the row's listed property is NOT predominantly used in a qualified business use, which is the condition IRC 280F(b)(1) attaches the alternative depreciation system to: the deduction allowed under section 168 for that year and every later year is determined under section 168(g), straight line over the ADS recovery period. It is the negation of the row's predominance test, so it measures the QUALIFIED business use percentage the taxpayer gives (IRC 280F(d)(6)(A)) and falls back to column (c) only where that is unanswered, and it is Incomplete until one of the two is answered.
WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT REACH. The printed line 27 block preprints S/L in column (g) for exactly this reason, and this fact is what tells a screen, a print binding or a reviewer that the row belongs there. It does not rewrite column (g): /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableMethodConvention stays a free String carrying the form's own spelling ("200 DB HY", "S/L MM"). The method itself is also asked as a typed code (/form4562ListedProperties/*/writableDepreciationMethod, vocabulary /form4562DepreciationMethodOptions), and a row this fact marks true whose typed method is not straight line blocks submission through /form4562AdsPropertyMethodIsNotStraightLine. The section 179 half of the same rule is enforced on /form4562ListedProperties/*/electedSection179CostAllowed.

Fact.Name: The business-use portion of a Part V row's cost (column (d) times column (c))
Fact.Description:
The part of the row's column (d) cost or other basis that is attributable to the business and investment use the taxpayer reports in column (c): the full basis multiplied by that whole-number percentage. It is the listed-property counterpart of the line 6 column (b) intake, which the Part I table takes as a cost "business use only" and Part V does not, and it is the ceiling IRC 179(c)(1)(A) puts on the row's column (i) election.
NOT COLUMN (e), and the difference is why this fact exists. Column (e) is defined as this same product REDUCED BY the section 179 expense and the special depreciation allowance already taken on the property, so bounding the section 179 election by column (e) would be circular — the operand would already have the answer subtracted out of it. This fact is the product before any such reduction, which is the quantity the statute measures the election against.
Incomplete until both column (c) and column (d) are answered; every consumer guards it with IsComplete so a half-entered row never moves another line.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's elected section 179 cost after the section 280F(a) passenger-automobile cap
Fact.Description:
The third and last of the three ceilings the row's column (i) passes through, applied to what the SUV stage left: on a row the taxpayer attests is a passenger automobile, an elected cost above the row's remaining section 280F(a) limit resolves to that limit. IRC 280F(d)(1) is explicit that a section 179 deduction on listed property is subject to the subsection (a) limitations "in the same manner as if it were a depreciation deduction allowable under section 168", so the luxury-automobile ceiling is a ceiling on the election and not only on the depreciation beside it.
THE CAP FIRES ONLY ON AN AFFIRMATIVE ATTESTATION AND AN AFFIRMATIVE CONTRADICTION. The taxpayer must have answered /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsPassengerAutomobile true, column (c) must be answered so the limit can be prorated, and the amount arriving from the SUV stage must be strictly greater than the remaining limit; anything else falls through term for term. A row with the attestation unanswered or answered no is NOT capped — the graph does not know the vehicle is a passenger automobile, and inventing an Incomplete there would blank the section 179 chain on every ordinary listed-property return.
BUT AN ATTESTED AUTOMOBILE WHOSE LIMIT DOES NOT RESOLVE IS NOT WAVED THROUGH. There is no catch-all here: once the row IS said to be a passenger automobile, this fact resolves only where /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnIRemainingLimit resolves. A blank column (c), or a claimed special depreciation allowance with no amount given for this automobile, therefore makes the row Incomplete rather than passing the uncapped figure up as a placeholder — the ceiling is the whole reason the attestation is asked, and a row that has one but cannot compute it has nothing to say.
PASSENGER AUTOMOBILE OUTRANKS SUV when a filer answers both attestations true, which is a contradiction the form cannot print: IRC 179(b)(5)(B)(i)(II) excludes from "sport utility vehicle" any vehicle that IS subject to section 280F, so the two populations do not overlap. This stage runs after the SUV stage and applies the lower of the two ceilings to such a row, which is the answer that cannot overstate the deduction.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's elected section 179 cost, bounded by that row's own business-use cost
Fact.Description:
The first of the three ceilings the row's column (i) passes through: the filer's entry, except that an entry exceeding the same row's business-use cost (column (d) multiplied by column (c)) resolves to that cost. IRC 179(c)(1)(A) requires the election to specify "the portion of the cost of such property" taken into account, and beyond the cost there is no portion left to elect — an amount larger than the property's own business-use cost is not a bigger election, it is not an election.
THIS IS THE LISTED-PROPERTY TWIN of /form4562Section179Properties/*/electedCostNotExceedingCost, which that fact's Description named as owed and left unbuilt because the operand it needed was not in the module. The operand is /form4562ListedProperties/*/businessUseCostOrOtherBasis, which is now, and which is deliberately not column (e): column (e) is that same product already reduced by the section 179 deduction, so bounding the election by it would be circular.
THE BOUND FIRES ONLY ON AN AFFIRMATIVE CONTRADICTION, and it is complete-safe. Column (c), column (d) and column (i) must all be answered AND column (i) must be strictly greater than the product before the bound arm is taken; equal entries and every ordinary entry fall through term for term, and a row with any of the three unanswered passes column (i)'s own completeness through unchanged.
A NOTE ON WHY THE ENGINE DOES NOT EXPRESS THIS AS A LIMIT. The natural spelling would be a Limit type="Max" on the column (i) writable reading the sibling cost, but a Limit body in this engine is a constant; no Limit anywhere in the dictionary reads a Dependency. A derived bound the totals read is therefore the only shape available, and it is the shape the line 6 twin already uses.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's elected section 179 cost after the section 179(b)(5) sport utility vehicle cap
Fact.Description:
The second of the three ceilings the row's column (i) passes through, applied to what the own-cost bound left: on a row the taxpayer attests is a sport utility vehicle within IRC 179(b)(5)(B), an elected cost above the year's SUV amount resolves to that amount. The statute writes the cap as a flat $25,000 and IRC 179(b)(6) indexes it; for a tax year beginning in 2025 the indexed figure is $31,300, which the Form 4562 instructions state twice.
WHAT THE ATTESTATION MEANS, because the graph cannot see a vehicle. /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableIsSection179Suv carries the whole of IRC 179(b)(5)(B): a 4-wheeled vehicle primarily designed or usable to carry passengers over public streets, rated at more than 6,000 and not more than 14,000 pounds gross vehicle weight, that is not itself subject to section 280F, and that is none of the three excluded shapes — more than nine seats behind the driver, a six-foot enclosed cargo area not reachable from the passenger compartment, or an integral cab-and-body enclosure with no rearward seating.
THE CAP FIRES ONLY ON AN AFFIRMATIVE ATTESTATION AND AN AFFIRMATIVE CONTRADICTION: the attestation must be answered true and the amount arriving from the own-cost stage must be strictly greater than the cap. A row with the attestation unanswered is not capped, which is the same complete-safe compromise the own-cost stage makes — the graph does not know the vehicle is an SUV, and a manufactured Incomplete would blank the section 179 chain for every filer who answers no question about a vehicle they do not own.

Fact.Name: A Part V row's column (i) elected section 179 cost as the law allows it to stand
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part V Section A column (i) for one listed-property row, after every ceiling the statute puts on it. This is the fact /form4562Line29ElectedSection179CostTotal sums, so it is what reaches Part I line 7, line 8, line 9 and the section 179 deduction on line 12; the raw column (i) intake is no longer added anywhere.
FOUR THINGS HAPPEN TO THE FILER'S ENTRY, in this order. It is bounded by the row's own business-use cost (IRC 179(c)(1)(A): there is no portion of the cost left to elect above the cost). It is capped at the sport utility vehicle amount when the taxpayer attests the vehicle is one (IRC 179(b)(5)). It is capped at what is left of the passenger-automobile limit when the taxpayer attests it is one (IRC 280F(a) through 280F(d)(1)). And it is zero outright on a row that is not predominantly used in a qualified business use, because IRC 280F(b) denies the section 179 election to such property altogether and the printed line 27 rows carry no column (i) box at all.
THE PREDOMINANCE TEST IS KEYED ON THE PERCENTAGE, NOT ON THE SLOT. The printed Part V table is two blocks of three fixed slots and the collection's positional convention puts the line 26 rows at items 0 to 2, but a convention is not an invariant: intake can place a 40 percent row in a line 26 position, and before this fact the line 29 total summed it in and the section 179 deduction grew by an amount no printed form permits. The gate here reads /form4562ListedProperties/*/isPredominantlyBusinessUse — which measures QUALIFIED business use (IRC 280F(d)(6)(A)) and not the business-and-investment percentage in column (c) — so the answer depends neither on where the row sits nor on use that is in column (c) but outside a trade or business.
A ROW WITH NO COLUMN (i) ENTRY HAS ELECTED NOTHING, AND IT RESOLVES TO ZERO. This is the FIRST case and it is the ordinary Part V row: listed property entered for depreciation only, whose columns (a) through (h) are filled in and whose column (i) box is blank. IRC 179(a) makes the deduction an election and IRC 179(c)(1)(A) makes the taxpayer specify, item by item, the portion of each item's cost taken into account — so a blank column (i) is not a missing operand, it is the absence of an election, and there is nothing for any ceiling below to bound. Such a row contributes $0 to line 29 and its column (h) depreciation is untouched. The case is tested ahead of the predominance zero as well as ahead of the settled-row guard, because a depreciation-only row characteristically answers neither vehicle question and gives no qualified-use percentage, so neither of those cases could reach it.
AN OPENED ROW WITH A BLANK REQUIRED BOX BLOCKS; IT DOES NOT PASS. "Opened", precisely, means the row CARRIES A COLUMN (i) ENTRY: that entry is the election, and the ceilings above cannot be applied to it until the boxes they read are answered — column (c), which prorates the section 280F(a) limit, the two vehicle questions, without which the graph cannot tell a $90,000 sport utility vehicle from a $90,000 machine tool, and the qualified business use percentage, without which the IRC 280F(b)(3) more-than-50-percent test cannot be passed (column (c) counts investment use and can only show the test failed, never that it is met). So this fact has NO catch-all. It resolves only where the row is settled — and a row with an election and a missing operand resolves to nothing at all, carrying that Incomplete up through line 29 to line 7, where a filer or a screen has to answer rather than receive a deduction the law may not allow. A column (i) answered $0.00 IS an election of zero and is an opened row on this test; that is the one boundary the blank-box case above does not cover, and it is intentional, since a filer who typed a zero has been through the box.
WHAT "SETTLED" MEANS, and why it is not simply all three boxes answered. IRC 179(b)(5)(B)(i)(II) makes the two vehicle categories disjoint — a sport utility vehicle for section 179(b)(5) is by definition not subject to section 280F — so ONE affirmative yes settles the row and the other question need not be asked. Two noes settle it as well. Anything less does not: one no with the other question unanswered leaves the vehicle unidentified. Demanding all three answers would instead refuse the sport utility vehicle row the filer HAS identified, which is why the test is a disjunction and not a conjunction.
A ROW THE PREDOMINANCE TEST ZEROES NEEDS NO ATTESTATION, because the answer is $0 whatever the vehicle is; that case settles the row on its own, and it is second only because the blank column (i) above reaches more rows.

Fact.Name: Predominant qualified business use for a Part V row (the more-than-50-percent test)
Fact.Description:
True exactly when the row's QUALIFIED business use percentage EXCEEDS 50 percent, which is the test IRC 280F(b)(3) writes for treating listed property as predominantly used in a qualified business use. Fifty percent itself is not predominant: the statute says "exceeds", and the printed form agrees, sending property used "50% or less" to the line 27 block.
THE OPERAND IS QUALIFIED BUSINESS USE, NOT COLUMN (c). IRC 280F(d)(6)(A) defines the "business use percentage" this test measures as the percentage of the property's use that is a QUALIFIED business use, and the Form 4562 instructions say outright that a filer's percentage of qualified business use may be smaller than the business/investment use percentage in column (c): investment use, leasing to a 5-percent owner or a related person, use as compensation that is not reported, and use non-deductible under section 274 all count in column (c) and none of them is a qualified business use. So this test reads /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableQualifiedBusinessUsePercentage wherever the filer has given it. Column (c) stays the operand of the two places the form measures business AND investment use — the section 280F(a) proration in /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnIRemainingLimit and the cost bound in /form4562ListedProperties/*/businessUseCostOrOtherBasis — and it is not this test.
COLUMN (c) IS THE FALLBACK, AND IT IS AN UPPER BOUND. Where the qualified percentage is unanswered this fact falls back to column (c), which can only be greater than or equal to the qualified percentage. A false answer from the fallback is therefore conclusive (column (c) at 50 percent or less means qualified use is too), and every consumer may act on it. A true answer from the fallback is not: a row whose column (c) exceeds 50 percent can have qualified business use that does not. So the section 179 election does not rest on it — /form4562ListedProperties/*/electedSection179CostAllowed requires the qualified percentage itself on an opened row and is Incomplete without it — and the interview MUST ask the question on any row above 50 percent that carries a column (i) election. The print-only consumers (/form4562ListedProperties/*/adsRequired, and the $20,200 arm of /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FFirstYearLimit, which takes the lower figure unless this fact is true) still read the fallback; the line 25 share still passes an entered amount on such a row (named residue).
IT IS ALSO THE FACT THE PART V CONVENTION WAS STANDING IN FOR. The collection's six slots are documented as line 26 rows at items 0 to 2 and line 27 rows at items 3 to 5, but nothing enforced that. Both the section 179 gate (/form4562ListedProperties/*/electedSection179CostAllowed) and the depreciation-system flag (/form4562ListedProperties/*/adsRequired) key on this fact rather than on the slot index, so a misfiled row gets the treatment its own percentage earns.
Incomplete until one of the two percentages is answered, and every consumer guards it with IsComplete so an unanswered percentage never zeroes an election or moves a total.

Fact.Name: What is left of a Part V row's section 280F(a) limit for its column (i) election
Fact.Description:
The ceiling IRC 280F(a) leaves for this row's elected section 179 cost: the first-year passenger-automobile limit for the tax year, reduced pro rata for business use below 100 percent, less the column (h) depreciation deduction and less the line 25 special depreciation allowance already claimed against the same limit for the same automobile, and never below zero.
THE LIMIT IS ONE POOL, NOT ONE PER COLUMN. The instructions are explicit that for any passenger automobile on line 26 or 27 the TOTAL of columns (h) and (i) on that line AND column (h) on line 25 for that automobile cannot exceed the applicable limit, so column (i) can only have what the other two have not taken. Both are subtracted here. A row whose column (h) and allowance already meet or exceed the limit leaves nothing, and this fact resolves to zero there rather than going negative.
THE FIRST-YEAR FIGURE IS THE RIGHT ONE for a section 179 election because IRC 179(a) allows the election only for the year the property is placed in service; a row that could reach a second, third or later-year figure in Table 2 has no column (i) entry to cap. For a passenger automobile placed in service in 2025 that is $12,200, or $20,200 where the taxpayer takes the special depreciation allowance for qualified property acquired after September 27, 2017. Which of the two applies is the taxpayer's own election, carried by /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableClaimsSpecialDepreciationAllowance; an unanswered attestation takes the lower, unbonused figure, which is the answer that cannot overstate the deduction.
THE HIGHER LIMIT IS NOT FREE, AND THE ARM THAT RAISES IT REFUSES TO RESOLVE WITHOUT ITS PRICE. The extra $8,000 in the $20,200 figure is IRC 168(k)(2)(F)'s increase for the very allowance the attestation claims, and that allowance is itself inside the pool the limit caps. An attestation of yes with no amount would therefore raise the ceiling by $8,000 and subtract nothing — the larger the bonus actually taken, the larger the overstatement, and under a 100 percent bonus a single automobile's allowance can exhaust the whole $20,200. So the amount is a required box on that arm: /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableSpecialDepreciationAllowanceAmount unanswered while the attestation is yes leaves this fact, and everything reading it, Incomplete rather than over-capped.
NAMED GAP. A row placed in service before 2025 takes no column (i) figure at all, so Tables 2 through 4's later-year rows are not modeled; that is visible only on a return that carries such a row, and it cannot raise the ceiling this fact sets.

Fact.Name: This Part V row's share of the printed line 25 special depreciation allowance
Fact.Description:
The IRC 168(k) special depreciation allowance this one listed-property row took, as a figure the printed line 25 total can be built out of: the row's own /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableSpecialDepreciationAllowanceAmount where the filer has given it, and $0 where the row took no allowance or was never asked.
WHY THE ZERO IS RIGHT AND NOT A GUESS. The Form 4562 instructions say to enter on line 25 the TOTAL special depreciation allowance for all qualified listed property, and Part V Section A lists that property row by row, so the total is the sum of the rows' own shares and a row that claims nothing adds nothing. Reading the raw writable straight into the sum would instead make line 25 - and through line 28, line 21 and line 22, the depreciation deduction itself - Incomplete on every return whose rows did not all answer an allowance box, which is nearly all of them. That is the complete-safe posture the empty-collection guards on /form4562Lines26And27ColumnHTotal and /form4562Line29ElectedSection179CostTotal already take for their own totals.
A ROW USED 50 PERCENT OR LESS IN A QUALIFIED BUSINESS USE TAKES NO ALLOWANCE, AND ITS SHARE IS ZERO WHATEVER WAS ENTERED. The printed line 25 is for listed property "used more than 50% in a qualified business use"; IRC 280F(b)(1) sends listed property that is not predominantly used in a qualified business use to the alternative depreciation system of section 168(g), and IRC 168(k)(2)(D) excludes from qualified property any property to which that system applies. So where /form4562ListedProperties/*/isPredominantlyBusinessUse resolves false the row's entered amount is not a lawful line 25 dollar and this fact is $0, in the same way the row's column (i) election is $0. The test is keyed on the QUALIFIED business use percentage where it is given and on column (c) otherwise, exactly as the predominance fact itself is; a row on which neither percentage is answered is not zeroed here, because that is a question the filer never reached.
A CLAIMED ALLOWANCE WITH NO AMOUNT BLOCKS LINE 25 RATHER THAN OMITTING ITSELF. Where the taxpayer has answered /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableClaimsSpecialDepreciationAllowance yes and the amount box is blank, this fact has no case and resolves to nothing, so line 25, line 28, line 21 and line 22 wait for the amount instead of printing a total that silently leaves out an allowance the filer said was taken. That is the same posture ../section280FColumnIRemainingLimit already takes for its own subtraction of this box, and it is an opened question with a required box blank, which may block; it does not touch line 29, because a row whose column (i) is blank still elects nothing. Everywhere the claim is no or unasked a blank amount is a row that took no allowance and adds $0.
ON A 2025 PASSENGER AUTOMOBILE THE SHARE STAYS INSIDE THE SECTION 280F(a) POOL. The Form 4562 instructions put the special depreciation allowance inside the passenger-automobile limit: the total of columns (h) and (i) on line 26 or 27 and column (h) on line 25 for that automobile cannot exceed the applicable limit. So on a row attested a passenger automobile and placed in service in 2025, an entered allowance above /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FFirstYearLimit resolves to that limit (a 100 percent allowance on a $60,000 automobile used wholly in the business is $20,200 here, not $60,000), and columns (h) and (i) then have nothing left. Every other row passes its amount through; an attested 2025 automobile whose limit cannot be computed (column (c) or the date blank) is Incomplete rather than carrying an uncapped allowance to line 25.
IT IS THE SAME FIGURE THE SECTION 280F(a) CAP SUBTRACTS, which is the whole point of asking it per row: /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnIRemainingLimit reads the writable directly, with its own no-catch-all guard, so an attested automobile that claims the allowance and gives no amount still blocks there. This fact does not soften that; it only supplies the addend line 25 needs.

Fact.Name: Basis for depreciation for a Part V row (column (e))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (e), the basis used for depreciation, business and investment use only: the column (d) cost multiplied by the column (c) percentage and reduced by any section 179 expense and special depreciation allowance already taken on the same property. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Business or investment use percentage for a Part V row (column (c))
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part V Section A column (c), the percentage of the property's use during the year that was business OR INVESTMENT use, as a whole number of percent. The percent sign is preprinted beside the box, so the Int prints bare.
IT IS NOT THE PREDOMINANT-USE TEST, and the difference matters. The instructions prorate the section 280F(a) passenger-automobile limit by this percentage and the business-use cost bound multiplies by it, which are the two things this box is for. Whether the row may be expensed under section 179 at all turns instead on the narrower QUALIFIED business use percentage that IRC 280F(d)(6)(A) defines, which is /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableQualifiedBusinessUsePercentage and can be smaller than this figure. The printed block a row belongs to — more than 50 percent on line 26, 50 percent or less on line 27 — is decided by that qualified percentage, not by this one.

Fact.Name: Special depreciation allowance claimed on a Part V passenger automobile
Fact.Description:
Ask on any Part V row the taxpayer has said is a passenger automobile: is the taxpayer claiming the special depreciation allowance on this automobile? Yes only for qualified property acquired after September 27, 2017 and placed in service this year for which the allowance has not been elected out of.
It picks which of the two first-year limits Form 4562's Table 2 sets for an automobile placed in service in 2025: $20,200 with the allowance, $12,200 without it. Answering no, or leaving it unanswered, takes the lower figure, so a filer who does not reach this question is never given the larger ceiling. It has no effect on a row that is not attested a passenger automobile.

Fact.Name: Cost or other basis for a Part V row (column (d))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (d), the full cost or other basis of the listed property, before the business use percentage is applied. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Date placed in service for a Part V row (column (b))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (b), the date the listed property was placed in service. It is a date, so it is held as a Day; unlike the Part III column (b) boxes this one prints a full date, so it needs no month and year transform.

Fact.Name: Depreciation deduction for a Part V row (column (h))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (h), the depreciation deduction for the row this year. Filer supplied for now: computing it needs a depreciable asset model that applies the row's method, recovery period and convention to the column (e) basis, which the graph does not have. The column (h) rows total into line 28.

Fact.Name: Elected section 179 cost for a Part V row (column (i))
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part V Section A column (i) for one listed-property row: the amount of this property's cost the taxpayer elects to expense under IRC 179. Only the line 26 rows print a column (i) box, because property used 50 percent or less in a qualified business use may not be expensed under section 179 at all.
THIS IS THE INTAKE, NOT THE ALLOWED AMOUNT. What the return acts on is /form4562ListedProperties/*/electedSection179CostAllowed, which is this entry after the ceilings the statute puts on it: the row's own business-use cost, the sport utility vehicle amount, the passenger-automobile limit, and zero where the property is not predominantly used in a qualified business use. Line 29 sums that fact, so an entry this box cannot support reaches no line of the return.

Fact.Name: The Part V row is a passenger automobile subject to the section 280F(a) limits
Fact.Description:
Ask on every Part V listed-property row: is this property a passenger automobile? Yes for a 4-wheeled vehicle manufactured primarily for use on public streets, roads and highways and rated at 6,000 pounds unloaded gross vehicle weight or less (for a truck or van, 6,000 pounds gross vehicle weight or less). No for an ambulance, a hearse or a vehicle used directly in the business of transporting persons or property for hire, and no for a heavier vehicle, which the section 280F(a) limits do not reach.
A yes caps this row's section 179 election and its depreciation at the year's luxury-automobile limit, prorated for the business-use percentage in column (c): for 2025 that is $12,200 in the first year, or $20,200 where the special depreciation allowance is claimed. The cap is what the law allows for the whole of columns (h) and (i) on this automobile together, so a large column (h) leaves less for column (i).
Answering no, or leaving the question unanswered, applies no automobile cap — the graph cannot see the vehicle and will not invent one. A vehicle over the section 280F weight thresholds is not a passenger automobile and may instead be a sport utility vehicle for section 179(b)(5), which is the next question.

Fact.Name: The Part V row is a sport utility vehicle within the section 179(b)(5) cap
Fact.Description:
Ask on every Part V listed-property row the taxpayer is electing section 179 on: is this vehicle a sport utility vehicle for the section 179 cap? Yes for a 4-wheeled vehicle primarily designed or usable to carry passengers over public streets, roads or highways, rated at more than 6,000 and not more than 14,000 pounds gross vehicle weight.
Answer no if the vehicle is any of the three the law excludes: one designed for a seating capacity of more than nine persons behind the driver; one with a cargo area of at least six feet of interior length, open or capped, that is not readily accessible directly from the passenger compartment; or one with an integral enclosure fully enclosing the driver compartment and load carrying device, with no seating rearward of the driver and no body section protruding more than 30 inches ahead of the windshield. Answer no as well for a lighter vehicle, which is a passenger automobile under the previous question instead — the two categories cannot both apply.
A yes caps the amount this row may elect under section 179 at $31,300 for a tax year beginning in 2025, however large the vehicle's cost. Answering no, or leaving the question unanswered, applies no SUV cap.

Fact.Name: Method and convention for a Part V row (column (g))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (g), the depreciation method and applicable convention as the form abbreviates them, for example 200 DB HY or S/L MM. The line 27 rows preprint S/L because listed property used 50 percent or less in a qualified business use must be depreciated straight line under the alternative depreciation system.

Fact.Name: Qualified business use percentage for a Part V row
Fact.Description:
Ask on any Part V listed-property row whose column (c) percentage is more than 50 percent and which carries a column (i) section 179 election: of the property's total use this year, what percentage was a QUALIFIED business use? A whole number of percent, and never more than the column (c) business/investment use percentage.
WHAT TO LEAVE OUT, and this is the whole point of the question: column (c) is business AND investment use, and qualified business use is narrower. Exclude use in an investment activity that is not a trade or business; exclude leasing the property to a 5-percent owner or a person related to one; exclude use as compensation to a 5-percent owner or a related person; exclude use as compensation to anyone else that was not reported on a Form W-2 or a Form 1099 and had no income tax withheld; and exclude use that is non-deductible under section 274. The Form 4562 instructions say plainly that the resulting percentage may be smaller than the column (c) percentage, and tell the filer to figure it the same way column (c) is figured.
WHY IT IS ASKED SEPARATELY. It is the operand of IRC 280F(b)(3)'s more-than-50-percent test — /form4562ListedProperties/*/isPredominantlyBusinessUse — which decides whether the row may be expensed under section 179 at all and whether IRC 280F(b)(1) sends its depreciation to the alternative depreciation system. Column (c) is not that operand: it is what the form prorates the section 280F(a) limit by and what the cost bound multiplies, and because it is the wider percentage it can be above 50 on a row whose qualified use is not.
Unanswered, the predominance test falls back to column (c), which is an upper bound on this figure: a row at 50 percent or less in column (c) is zeroed without asking, correctly. On a row above 50 percent that carries a column (i) election the answer is REQUIRED: /form4562ListedProperties/*/electedSection179CostAllowed, line 29 and line 7 are Incomplete until it is given, because column (c) above 50 cannot show that qualified use is (without it the row would keep an election the statute may deny). That is why the interview asks this on every such row rather than deferring it. There is no printed box for it — the form asks the filer to place the row in the line 26 or line 27 block, and this is the figure that placement rests on.

Fact.Name: Recovery period for a Part V row (column (f))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (f), the recovery period the row uses, printed as the form prints it. It is a String and not an Int because the box carries the form's own spelling, such as 5 or 27.5.

Fact.Name: The line 25 special depreciation allowance taken on one Part V listed-property row
Fact.Description:
Ask on any Part V Section A row: how much of the line 25 special depreciation allowance did the taxpayer take on THIS item of listed property? A dollar amount. It is asked on every row, not only on vehicles, because line 25 is the total allowance for ALL qualified listed property, and it is the box the interview MUST reach on a row the taxpayer has said is a passenger automobile and is claiming the allowance on.
IT IS WHAT PRINTED LINE 25 IS MADE OF. /form4562Line25ListedPropertySpecialAllowance sums these shares over the whole table through /form4562ListedProperties/*/specialDepreciationAllowanceShare, so the printed total is exactly what its own rows add to and cannot be stated independently of them. A row that took no allowance leaves the box blank and adds nothing.
AND IT IS THE THIRD TERM OF THE SECTION 280F(a) CAP, which is why it is asked per item rather than once. The Form 4562 instructions cap one pool, not three: for any passenger automobile listed on line 26 or 27, the total of columns (h) and (i) on that line AND column (h) on line 25 for that automobile cannot exceed the applicable limit. Without the per-item share, the attestation that lifts a row's ceiling from $12,200 to $20,200 would raise the ceiling by exactly the allowance it claims and subtract nothing.
LEAVING IT BLANK BLOCKS RATHER THAN PASSES ON AN AUTOMOBILE THAT CLAIMS THE ALLOWANCE. Where the taxpayer has said yes to the allowance on an attested passenger automobile, /form4562ListedProperties/*/section280FColumnIRemainingLimit does not resolve until this box is answered, and the Incomplete carries up through the row's allowed elected cost to line 29 and line 7. On ANY row where the claim is answered yes and this box is blank, line 25 waits as well: /form4562ListedProperties/*/specialDepreciationAllowanceShare has no case for that pair, so the printed total does not silently omit an allowance the filer said was taken. Everywhere else a blank box is simply a row that took no allowance: it subtracts nothing and it adds nothing to line 25. An amount entered on a row used 50 percent or less in a qualified business use is not a line 25 dollar and the share is $0 there. Zero is a legitimate answer and means the allowance on this item was nil.

Fact.Name: Type of listed property for a Part V row (column (a))
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A column (a), the type of property the row covers, vehicles listed first. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 Section B vehicles
Fact.Description: The vehicles whose use Form 4562 Part V Section B reports: vehicles used by a sole proprietor, partner or other more than 5 percent owner, or a related person. Section B prints SIX FIXED COLUMNS, Vehicle 1 through Vehicle 6, so one item per printed column in that order (item 0 is column (a) Vehicle 1 and item 5 is column (f) Vehicle 6), an item left blank when the column is unused. That positional convention is what the IRS4562 /form4562Vehicles columns axis declares, and intake must create the columns in that order.

Fact.Name: No other vehicle available for personal use
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 36 for this vehicle: the negation of the other vehicle attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: Vehicle not available for personal use off duty
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 34 for this vehicle: the negation of the off duty personal use attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: Vehicle not used primarily by a more than 5 percent owner
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 4562 line 35 for this vehicle: the negation of the more than 5 percent owner attestation, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked.

Fact.Name: Vehicle total miles driven
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 line 33 for this vehicle: total miles driven during the year, the sum of the line 30 business and investment miles, the line 31 commuting miles and the line 32 other personal miles. The printed line states that arithmetic, so it is COMPUTED here rather than taken.
This fact replaces the former intake /form4562Vehicles/*/writableTotalMilesDriven, which duplicated the three mileage leaves it is printed beside and could therefore disagree with its own components: a filer could type 12,000 plus 3,000 plus 1,000 on lines 30 to 32 and 20,000 on line 33 and nothing in the graph objected. The addition is written out below with an inline complete safe leg per component, the same shape the Schedule 1-A line 14c sum uses.
COMPLETE SAFE PER LEG, INCOMPLETE WHEN THE COLUMN IS BLANK. Each of the three legs reads its intake when answered and 0 when it is not, so a vehicle column that fills only some of lines 30 to 32 still foots. The fall through arm is reached only when all three are unanswered, and it resolves to the unanswered line 30 intake, which keeps this fact Incomplete so the printed line 33 box stays blank on a vehicle row the filer never mileage answered rather than printing a manufactured 0.
NO COMMITTED FIGURE MOVES: the one node fixture that answered the old intake set 12,000 plus 3,000 plus 1,000 against a typed 16,000 and 4,500 plus 0 plus 500 against a typed 5,000, both of which this sum reproduces exactly.

Fact.Name: Vehicle business or investment miles driven
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 30 for this vehicle: total business and investment miles driven during the year, not counting commuting miles. Taxpayer supplied from the vehicle mileage records that section 274(d) requires for listed property.

Fact.Name: Vehicle commuting miles driven
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 31 for this vehicle: total commuting miles driven during the year. Commuting is not a use in a trade or business, so these miles are outside the vehicle's qualified business use.

Fact.Name: Another vehicle available for personal use
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 36 for this vehicle, the Yes box: is another vehicle available for the user's personal use? The answer bears on whether this vehicle's personal use is substantiated.

Fact.Name: Vehicle available for personal use off duty
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 34 for this vehicle, the Yes box: was the vehicle available for personal use during off duty hours? A vehicle available for personal use has use that is not a use in the taxpayer's trade or business.

Fact.Name: Vehicle used primarily by a more than 5 percent owner
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 35 for this vehicle, the Yes box: was the vehicle used primarily by a more than 5 percent owner or a related person? Such use is excluded from qualified business use.

Fact.Name: Vehicle other personal miles driven
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 32 for this vehicle: total other personal, noncommuting, miles driven during the year. Personal use is not a use in a trade or business, so these miles are outside the vehicle's qualified business use.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 23a basis attributable to capitalized section 263A interest
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part IV line 23a: for assets shown in Part III that were placed in service during the tax year and have costs capitalized under section 263A, the amount of the basis attributable to interest costs capitalized under IRC 263A(f). It is a memorandum figure that no other printed line consumes. Filer supplied: the graph has no depreciable asset model and no uniform capitalization computation.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 23b basis attributable to other capitalized section 263A costs
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part IV line 23b: for assets shown in Part III that were placed in service during the tax year and have costs capitalized under section 263A, the amount of the basis attributable to costs capitalized under IRC 263A other than the interest costs line 23a reports. Filer supplied for the same reason as line 23a.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 24a evidence supporting the claimed business use
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A line 24a: true when the taxpayer has evidence to support the business or investment use of the listed property claimed in the line 26 and 27 rows. The Yes box prints when this is true and the No box prints when it is false. Filer supplied: it is an attestation about the taxpayer's own records, which the graph does not hold.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 24b written evidence
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A line 24b: true when the evidence the taxpayer answered Yes to on line 24a is written. The Yes box prints when this is true and the No box prints when it is false. The form asks line 24b only of a taxpayer who answered Yes on line 24a. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 24c aircraft chartered
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A line 24c Charter box: true when the taxpayer charters an aircraft. One of the three independent check all that apply boxes on line 24c. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 24c aircraft leased
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A line 24c Lease box: true when the taxpayer leases an aircraft. One of the three independent check all that apply boxes on line 24c. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 24c aircraft owned
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A line 24c Own box: true when the taxpayer owns an aircraft. Line 24c is a check all that apply question, so the three boxes are three independent Bools rather than one enumeration. Filer supplied.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 25 special depreciation allowance for listed property
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part V Section A line 25, the IRC 168(k) additional first year allowance for qualified listed property placed in service during the tax year and used more than 50 percent in a qualified business use. RETIRED: the return computes line 25 from the Part V table at /form4562Line25ListedPropertySpecialAllowance, the sum of the per-row /form4562ListedProperties/*/specialDepreciationAllowanceShare figures, and nothing reads this intake. It keeps its path and its meaning for intake that has already collected an answer here; a filer with a figure for this box has listed property, and the figure belongs on the Part V Section A rows it was taken on, where the same amount also reduces each automobile's section 280F(a) ceiling.

Fact.Name: Written policy prohibiting all personal use of vehicles
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 37, the Yes box: do you maintain a written policy statement that prohibits all personal use of vehicles, including commuting, by your employees? A Yes is one of the exceptions that relieves an employer from completing Section B for the covered vehicles.

Fact.Name: Written policy prohibiting personal use except commuting
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 38, the Yes box: do you maintain a written policy statement that prohibits personal use of vehicles, except commuting, by your employees? A Yes is one of the exceptions that relieves an employer from completing Section B for the covered vehicles.

Fact.Name: All employee vehicle use treated as personal use
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 39, the Yes box: do you treat all use of vehicles by employees as personal use? A Yes is one of the exceptions that relieves an employer from completing Section B for the covered vehicles.

Fact.Name: More than five vehicles provided and use information retained
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 40, the Yes box: do you provide more than five vehicles to your employees, obtain information from your employees about the use of the vehicles, and retain the information received? A Yes is one of the exceptions that relieves an employer from completing Section B for the covered vehicles.

Fact.Name: Qualified automobile demonstration use requirements met
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 41, the Yes box: do you meet the requirements concerning qualified automobile demonstration use? A Yes is one of the exceptions that relieves an employer from completing Section B for the covered vehicles.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 line 43 amortization from prior years
Fact.Description: Form 4562 line 43: amortization of costs that began before the 2025 tax year. Taxpayer supplied because the graph carries no prior year amortization schedule.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 depreciation method codes
Fact.Description: The four method codes the 2025 Form 4562 instructions print for the Part III column (f) and Part V column (g) method boxes: 200 DB, 150 DB, S/L, and PRE (ACRS prescribed percentages for property placed in service before 1987, Part V only). The typed vocabulary behind /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableDepreciationMethod, /form4562Assets/*/writableDepreciationMethod and /form4562AdsAssets/*/writableDepreciationMethod.

Fact.Name: Property that must use the alternative depreciation system is given a method other than straight line
Fact.Description: You gave a depreciation method other than straight line (S/L) for property that must be depreciated under the alternative depreciation system: a Part V listed-property row not used more than 50 percent in a qualified business use (/form4562ListedProperties/*/adsRequired), or a Part III Section C row. The alternative depreciation system uses the straight line method, and the form preprints S/L on those rows. Change the method to S/L, then check the depreciation you entered. TRUE when such a row answers /form4562ListedProperties/*/writableDepreciationMethod or /form4562AdsAssets/*/writableDepreciationMethod with any code but straightLine; Complete false otherwise, including every row whose method is unanswered and every return without those tables. A submission block for a contradiction in the filer's own answers, not a scope refusal.

Fact.Name: Depreciation method for a Part V row (column (g), method half)
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Which depreciation method did you use?" with the four printed codes as choices: 200 DB (200 percent declining balance), 150 DB (150 percent declining balance), S/L (straight line) and, for listed property placed in service before 1987 only, PRE (the ACRS prescribed percentages). HELP TEXT: the Form 4562 instructions name exactly these codes for the method column. Column (g) prints method and convention together; this is the method alone, typed. Property used 50 percent or less in a qualified business use must use S/L over its ADS recovery period. ASKED WHEN: every Part V Section A row. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; the free-text method box (/form4562ListedProperties/*/writableMethodConvention) still prints, and no check below runs on an unanswered row. VALIDATION: one of the four enum values of /form4562DepreciationMethodOptions. WHAT IT FEEDS: /form4562AdsPropertyMethodIsNotStraightLine (with /form4562ListedProperties/*/adsRequired).

Fact.Name: Depreciation method for a Part III Section B row (column (f))
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Which depreciation method did you use?" with the four printed codes as choices: 200 DB (200 percent declining balance), 150 DB (150 percent declining balance), S/L (straight line) and, for listed property placed in service before 1987 only, PRE (the ACRS prescribed percentages). HELP TEXT: the Form 4562 instructions name exactly these codes for the method column. The method is prescribed for each classification, with an irrevocable election of straight line for a whole classification. ASKED WHEN: every Part III Section B row. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; the free-text method box (/form4562Assets/*/writableMethod) still prints, and no check below runs on an unanswered row. Fact.Name: Form 4562 was answered (the filer opened the form)
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Form 4562, and an ANSWERED-NESS predicate in the shape form1116:/form1116Answered set: true when the filer opened any intake this form owns — a ROW in one of the five Part I/III/V/VI tables (/form4562Section179Properties, /form4562Assets, /form4562AdsAssets, /form4562ListedProperties, /form4562AmortizedCosts), the Form 4562 header's business-or-activity name (/writableForm4562BusinessOrActivity), one of the four scalar lines that can foot line 22 on their own (Part II lines 14, 15 and 16 and Part III line 17), or the Part I line 10 carryover of a section 179 deduction disallowed in an earlier year (/writableForm4562Line10CarryoverFromPriorYear).
LINE 10 IS A LEG because the second Who Must File bullet names it: a section 179 expense deduction "(which may include a carryover from a previous year)". A filer whose only Form 4562 entry is the carryover still claims it on line 12 or carries what line 11 disallows to line 13, and both are printed only on this form. LINE 15 IS A LEG for the same reason lines 14 and 16 are: it is an addend of line 22 that no table carries. The retired line 7 intake (/writableForm4562Line7ListedPropertyElectedCost) is NOT a leg: nothing reads it, line 7 is computed from the Part V table, and that table's own leg already turns the form on whenever line 7 can be non-zero. AN EMPTY BUT CREATED COLLECTION READS AS NOT ANSWERED, measured rather than argued: js/src/setupFactGraph.ts lines 182-187 (and its twin at 251-254) — the production JS path — SEEDS AN EMPTY COLLECTION for every writable Collection fact on a return that persists no /filers, so a bare IsComplete over one of these five tables is TRUE on a return that opened nothing, and the render gate printed Form 4562 on every such return. Each of the five collection legs is therefore a PRESENCE test inside an IsComplete guard — qbi:/qbiHasPatronBusiness's idiom, and the same IsComplete-plus-CollectionSize pair /form4562Line7ListedPropertyElectedCost already uses one page above. The guard keeps the predicate Complete on a return that never initialised the table (an absent collection resolves Complete FALSE here, never Incomplete); CollectionSize inside the guarded arm makes an answered-but-empty table read FALSE. The four scalar legs are untouched: IsComplete on an unanswered scalar writable is Complete FALSE already, and the same holds for the line 10 and line 15 legs.
WHY NOT A VALUE TEST. The printed rule is a list of claims — "Except as otherwise noted, complete and file Form 4562 if you are claiming any of the following: Depreciation for property placed in service during the 2025 tax year; A section 179 expense deduction (which may include a carryover from a previous year); Depreciation on any vehicle or other listed property (regardless of when it was placed in service); ... Amortization of costs that begins during the 2025 tax year" — and the natural value test, line 22 greater than zero, cannot serve as a render gate here: /form4562Line22TotalDepreciation is an Add straight over the raw line 14/15/16/17 writables, so it is INCOMPLETE on every return that never opened Form 4562, and a gate that answers Incomplete leaves the filler with no answer about whether the form is in the return at all. Line 22 is also silent on the third bullet, which is a PRESENCE rule ("regardless of when it was placed in service"): a listed property whose current-year deduction is $0 still obliges the form. IsComplete resolves Complete on every return, so this predicate is complete-safe by construction.
NOTE (per-activity multiplicity): the instructions say "File a separate Form 4562 for each business or activity", and the TY2025 register dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS4562 maps one copy's root paths. One printed copy is what this gate turns on; the per-activity copy is a named successor.

Fact.Name: The Form 4562 basis of refueling property is already reduced by its Form 8911 credit
Fact.Description: Is the basis for depreciation you entered on Form 4562 (column (c)) for your alternative fuel vehicle refueling property already reduced by the credit figured for that property on Form 8911 (Schedule A lines 16 plus 21, shown as its basis reduction)? Asked when Form 8911 applies and you depreciate the property on Form 4562. Answering no blocks the return from being submitted until the basis entered on Form 4562 is reduced. UNANSWERED IS DEFAULTED: the entered basis is used as entered and nothing is blocked, so an unasked question leaves an unreduced basis, and overstated depreciation, undetected.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 depreciation is claimed on a basis the filer says is not reduced by the Form 8911 credit
Fact.Description: You said the basis for depreciation you entered on Form 4562 for your alternative fuel vehicle refueling property is not reduced by its Form 8911 credit. The law reduces that basis by the credit, so depreciation figured on the unreduced basis is overstated. Enter the reduced basis on Form 4562, then answer the question again. TRUE when Form 8911 applies and /writableForm4562BasisReducedByForm8911Credit is answered no; complete false otherwise, including when the question is unanswered. A submission block for a contradiction in the filer's own answers, not a scope refusal.
